text:
Marta: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak we started seeing long-seq tenants pulling KV-prefetch budgets and pushing short requests into 200ms+ tails. Noticed on canary cluster around 06:30 UTC.
Ryan: ugh — saw p95 jump in the canary perf dashboard? numbers? :eyes:
Marta: p50 stable, p95 for short sequences went from 42ms -> 210ms, p99 ~ 480ms. KV hit rate for short requests dropped from 86% -> 55%. Token throughput unchanged.
Sophia: do we have trace snippets? can you paste a small flame or perf log?
Marta: pasted minimal trace below 
```
# sample from /var/log/batcher/profile.log
batch_id=8243 tenant=alpha seq_len=1024 kernel=fastpath slots=2 tokens=1024 kv_hit=false
batch_id=8244 tenant=beta seq_len=32 kernel=slowpath slots=8 tokens=32 kv_hit=true
... (repeats)
```
Marta: pattern: long seqs get prioritized kernel that keeps them pinned and they cold-evict KV entries used by short seqs. Fairness imbalance.
Leo: so kernel selection + batch formation ordering -> priority inversion. Could we tweak queue admission to prefer shorter seq when KV_hit_prob falls?
TJ: proposal: quota-equilibrium circuit-breaker — dynamic per-tenant token caps that shrink long-seq allocation when short-path tail increases. Also a KV-health signal that triggers preemptive lane smoothing.
Ryan: interesting. how would the circuit-breaker arm/unarm? thresholds?
TJ: start simple: if short-path p95 > 3x baseline OR KV_hit_short < 70% for 5min then cap long-seq token budget to 40% of default for that tenant for 60s. After cap period we gradually ramp back.
Sophia: need to avoid oscillation. suggest adding a hysteresis window + a jittered backoff on ramp. Also track kernel swap counts per-GPU to avoid thrash.
Marta: agreed. Also add an early-warning metric: "kv-displacement-rate" measuring unique KV keys evicted by other tenants per minute.
Leo: any perf regression risk from the cap itself? if we cap long seqs too aggressively throughput for those tenants will drop. rollout plan?
TJ: A/B canary: 5% of hosts with breaker enabled, 10% tenants selected having mixed long/short. Monitor p50/p95 short, p50 long, overall token/sec and tail latency. If short p95 improves and overall QPS delta < 2% then promote. Rollback if short p95 doesn't improve or long p50 degrades > 15%.
Marta: i'm adding a small instrumented variant in the runtime: `quota_breaker_v1` that exposes debug counters and exposes an endpoint `/debug/quota_breaker/state` per-host.
Sophia: please include the following metrics in the dashboard tile: short_p95_by_tenant, kv_hit_short_pct, kv_displacement_rate, kernel_swap_rate, breaker_state_rate.
Ryan: who can run the canary and watch the first 30m? i'll volunteer to watch infra alarms. Marta can you deploy?
Marta: i'll push the feature branch and create a canary job for tonight's 02:00 PDT window. tagging infra-bot to schedule.
infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: cluster=canary-westus1 start=2026-03-19T09:00:00Z hosts=12 config=quota_breaker_v1. :white_check_mark:
Leo: quick note — add a safety override so SLO-critical tenants can opt-out via tenant config `priority_override=true`. Don't want auto-cap on enterprise critical paths.
Marta: good call, will include opt-out gate and require admin flag.
TJ: experiment checklist: (1) rollout 5% hosts, (2) smoke 10 tenants, (3) collect 30m baseline + 60m with breaker, (4) analyze p50/p95/p99 + kv metrics, (5) decision. I'll document in the experiment runbook.
Sophia: also snapshot kernel selector weights before deploy so we can revert kernels independently.
Marta: created issue in backlog and linked the runbook. I'll post a follow-up with the PR and the run id once ready. Thanks all. :+1:
Ryan: thanks — see you in the post-canary sync.
TJ: ping me if you want the circuit-breaker sim script, i can share.
Marta: will do.
